body:
# Independent audit: the attained outward-smoothed H interface

Audited `candidate 0fa64553cd01d7ae`, including the updated uniform kernel and full ambient-roof construction. The construction passes within its explicitly stated compact positive-fiber minimal-bad-body framework. It constructs a stronger actual variational interface; it does not itself establish the sharp numerical payment.

## 1. Smoothing, compactness, and source geometry

The uniform CDF is continuous and Lipschitz. For every nonzero continuous normal its two corner hyperplanes have zero d-volume on each positive d-dimensional fiber. Dominated differentiation gives the displayed C1 cap-parameter derivatives. Moving-parameter continuity of those derivatives follows from the same zero-volume fact. Body-shape differentiation needs only continuity of the CDF. No hidden second derivative is used.

The outward inequality beta_(epsilon,h)>=beta_epsilon^H>=beta_0 holds before normalization and therefore legitimately places a minimizing sequence in the previously proved compact bad sublevel. The subsequent O(h) slab estimate is used on that compact class rather than circularly used to create compactness. Its constants are uniform in arbitrary base tilts because a base tilt only translates the continuous cutting plane separately on each fiber.

Compactly supported transition values permit exact clipping of base tilts. The own source ball supplies a uniformly positive slab coarea after Gamma normalization, so the quantile is locally strictly decreasing and the active menus are attained. The strict pure-base reserve persists after the O(h) perturbation.

The source-base moment identity m_base=S p is exact. At an integer convex combination of deepest marks, concavity of f and strictness of the attaining quantile force the SAME cap and threshold at every positive endpoint. Its one positive kernel measure cannot have two different base centroids. This proves that the source hull is an empty lattice polytope, including its boundary, and hence that its source vertices have distinct parity. Strict own-fiber concavity gives one mark per source base. None of these strict conclusions is silently transferred to new deepest marks in the zero-width limit.

## 2. Actual cover and first response

For the finite own-source menu, the tangent inequality for the strictly concave f gives a nonnegative cover function with unique interior zero. Its actual contact minimum can therefore be differentiated at this SINGLE old source. Equalizing the smooth cap masses through the weighted threshold equation covers the entire current source fiber: a nonnegative weighted margin forces at least one individual through-mark threshold above that cap's equalized threshold, and its mass is therefore no greater than the equalized mass. The finite off-source gap supplies the global upper cover.

I independently recomputed the captured-volume LOSS:

    L_j=B_j+S_j r_j-m_j.nu_j+A_j dot Gamma_j.

The negative sign in A_j is important. With Gamma(u)=1,

    dot Gamma=(D-J_j)/(2M)+grad Gamma.dot u,

so the effective moment is m_j-A_j(0,grad Gamma), exactly as stated. Weighted inverse coareas yield the denominator B_i=sum rho_ij/S_ij and the exact linear singleton response. There is no residual contact minimum or omitted inside hinge at positive width.

The actual additive convex-field cone and signed normal variables admit the finite-field separation/FIP construction. The resulting normalization satisfies sum omega_ij=1. Recombining the H response and width response gives precisely

    covariance coefficient e_i rho_ij-omega_ij A_ij,
    constant correction +Abar/(2M).

Thus the covariance coefficient is nonnegative and the target constant is beta+(d+2)Delta/(2dM)-Abar/(2M). Both the signs and the units check. The signed normal equations reproduce m/S=Y-[epsilon f-A/S](0,grad Gamma), including the same base centroid.

Since -hS<=A<=0, bounded section coareas give O(h) width errors uniformly on the normal bundle. Positive source cores, bounded inverse coareas, and the simplex normalization give Delta comparable to epsilon. Accordingly the relative width error is O(h/epsilon), as claimed; eliminating it does not eliminate the supporting selectors.

## 3. The zero-width Gauss--Green limit

The selected cap counts, source bases, normalized continuous normals, clipped base tilts, and all nonnegative coefficient vectors admit one common subsequence. Uniform cap-mass approximation proves that the limiting selected caps have the original raw critical mass, while continuity and attainment give an actual H-minimizing limiting body.

Boundary-capture measures are dominated by the corresponding convergent fiber surface measures on the normal bundle. Their limits therefore have densities in [0,1]. The smooth section measures have uniformly bounded mass and lie in vanishing slabs. Gauss--Green passes with compact C1 tests using the joint normal-bundle convergence, not an assumed pointwise convergence of facet normals.

At outside support the volume term tends to zero and the outer facet normal is +u/|u|. Thus the section density is W/|u|. At inside support the volume term tends to the full fiber integral and the outer normal is -u/|u|; subtraction of ordinary Gauss--Green yields (1-W)/|u|. If the contact set has zero facet area, domination of the boundary measure gives zero supporting section mass. A proper cutting plane gives the ordinary full section coarea. These arguments include d=1, where facet area is counting measure.

The limiting separator is obtained by passing its inequalities. It does not rely on the retained menus covering additional deepest bases that may emerge in the limit. This is the correct limiting scope.

## 4. Shared roofs and the uniform-kernel convex lifts

On a compact patch in a limiting own facet, positive-fiber Hausdorff convergence gives a common inward point on each transverse line and therefore an actual concave upper boundary graph. The graph heights tend uniformly to zero. On a slightly smaller patch, concavity controls all tangential slopes by the uniform height oscillation, so graph area densities tend to one.

CDF symmetry changes an inside supporting capture into its section complement. After this sign change, every section selector has the form Psi(alpha r+ell), with the SAME concave roof r and alpha>0. For the uniform CDF this is min(1,(1+alpha r+ell)_+). Its positive support is convex and its restriction to that support is concave. The bounded hypograph lift with 0<=t<=1 and t<=1+alpha r+ell is convex. Hausdorff convergence of compact convex lifts gives volume/L1 convergence even when the limiting lift is lower-dimensional.

For one full ambient facet, the proof retains sampled bases on its projection boundary. Each compact own-facet patch has a uniform inward line segment in its positive sampled fiber. The common roof is consequently defined on all those patches, and concavity defines it on their convex hull G. The lower roof bound extends by convex combinations; the global limiting supporting plane and ambient Hausdorff convergence give the uniform upper bound. This proves the stated JOINT concave roof without discarding ambient-surface-null sampled traces.

The finite sampled traces of the bounded lifts can be extracted simultaneously. Their actual anchored Minkowski inclusions pass to the limit, and their continuous volumes converge, including zero-volume limiting traces. This avoids the invalid substitution of ambient surface measure for the mixed fiber-sum measure. The construction is local to one ambient facet and makes no unsupported cross-facet gluing claim.

Finally, exact equal/opposite normalized continuous normals give the displayed order relations between CDF values. The note correctly requires finite-width equality or controlled scaled offsets; equality of limiting normals alone is insufficient.

## 5. Scope retained by this audit

No repair is needed. Two boundaries of the theorem remain essential: (i) an individual convex height lift for each cap is not yet ONE common convex body whose ordinary halfspace caps realize the whole menu, because saturation is a cap-dependent slab operation; (ii) the positive-width parity sources need not cover all newly deepest bases of the zero-width limit. The note respects both distinctions. The sharp Gamma_d/k(P) payment is still a separate obligation.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
